(Capacity: 13,819) | champion = | tourney = [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Final Four }} {{2020–21 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 NCAA Division I season]]. The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] were led by second-year head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]] and played their home games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. [[Tyger Campbell]] was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]], while [[Jaime Jaquez Jr.]] and [[Johnny Juzang]] were selected second-team All-Pac-12. Jaquez also earned Pac-12 All-Defensive team honors. Prior to the season, five-star recruit [[Daishen Nix]] decommitted from his [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] with UCLA to sign instead with the [[NBA G League]].{{cite news|title=UCLA recruit Daishen Nix decommits from Bruins, signs with G League|date=April 28, 2020|newspaper=The Canton Repository|url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20200428/ucla-recruit-daishen-nix-decommits-from-bruins-signs-with-g-league|access-date=April 2, 2021}} Picked by the media to win the conference, the Bruins were 6–2 to start the season when senior [[Chris Smith (basketball, born 1999)|Chris Smith]] suffered a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn anterior cruciate ligament]] in the win against [[2020–21 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title= UCLA beats Colorado after learning Chris Smith has torn ACL, will miss rest of season|date=January 2, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url= https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-01-02/ucla-basketball-colorado-chris-smith-torn-acl|access-date=January 2, 2021}} Their best player, who was the Pac-12 Most Improved Player and a first-team All-Pac-12 selection the season prior, was ruled out for the season.{{cite news|first=Billy|last=Witz|title=Meet the New U.C.L.A.: Plucky Underdog|date=March 29, 2021|newspaper=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/29/sports/ncaabasketball/ucla-michigan-ncaa-tournament.html|access-date=March 30, 2021}}{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA's star-starved team struggling to stay near top of Pac-12|date=February 12, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-02-12/ucla-men-basketball-struggles-pac-12-washington-state|access-date=March 30, 2021}} The Bruins began [[2020–21 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 conference play]] with a 5–0 record after beating [[Arizona–UCLA men's basketball rivalry|rival]] [[2020–21 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] on the road. This marked the fourth consecutive time UCLA had beaten Arizona in [[Tucson, Arizona|Tucson]]; it was also their fourth straight win against the Wildcats overall, making this the longest win streak by either team in the series since 2009.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Tyger Campbell makes UCLA stand tall in victory at Arizona|date=January 9, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-01-09/ucla-hangs-on-for-win-at-arizona-improves-to-5-0-in-pac-12|access-date=January 10, 2021}} UCLA extended their conference record to 8–0 with a 61–57 road win against [[2020–21 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]]. It was their best conference start since opening 9–0 in [[1982–83 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1982–83]], and the Bruins improved to 12–2 overall,{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title= UCLA extends Pac-12 unbeaten streak with narrow victory over Cal|date=January 21, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-01-21/ucla-mens-basketball-california-pac-12|access-date=January 22, 2021}} including 7–0 in games decided by five points or less or which went into overtime.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Finally left at a loss, UCLA must seek answers after Stanford heartbreak|date=September 24, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-01-24/ucla-mens-basketball-stanford-loss-pac-12|access-date=January 25, 2021}} In their following game against [[2020–21 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]], they suffered their first Pac-12 defeat after surrendering a buzzer-beating [[layup]] on an inbounds pass in a 73–72 overtime loss.{{cite January after his prep season was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Freshman Mac Etienne goes from prep school to early riser for UCLA|date=February 9, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-02-09/freshman-mac-etienne-early-riser-ucla|access-date=March 11, 2021}} UCLA ended the regular season losing three straight. They lost the regular season finale 64–63 to [[2020–21 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]], who made a game-winning [[three-point field goal]] with 1.4 seconds left in the game. The Bruins led by 11 at halftime and were up by eight with five minutes remaining. The loss ended their 18-game home winning streak and extended the Trojans' winning streak in [[UCLA–USC rivalry|their crosstown rivalry]] to four. UCLA played the game without their leading scorer, Juzang, who sprained his ankle.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA hopes to leave Las Vegas having purged its recent sins|date=March 9, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-03-09/ucla-basketball-struggles-pac-12-tournament-ncaa|access-date=March 10, 2021}} The Bruins ended with a 13–6 conference record to earn the No. 4 seed in the [[2021 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Tahj Eaddy scores just before buzzer to lift USC to stunning comeback win over UCLA|date=March 6, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2021-03-06/tahj-eaddy-usc-basketball-comeback-ucla-pac-12|access-date=March 7, 2021}} In their tourney opener in the quarterfinals, they lost 83–79 in overtime to [[2020–21 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]] after leading by as many as 16 in the first half and holding a 10-point advantage at halftime. It was their fourth consecutive loss after blowing a second-half lead. Juzang returned from his injury and scored 12 points.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA collapses late again in overtime loss to Oregon State in Pac-12 tournament|date=March 11, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-03-11/ucla-overtime-loss-oregon-state-pac-12-tournament|access-date=March 11, 2021}} UCLA was selected for the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], opening in the First Four against [[2020–21 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. In a reversal, the Bruins trailed by as many as 14 in the first half and 11 at halftime before rallying to win 86–80 in overtime. Jaquez finished with a career-high 27 points in UCLA's first NCAA tournament win since [[2016–17 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2017]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA surges late to defeat Michigan State in First Four overtime thriller|date=March 18, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles underdog, the largest Final Four [[point spread]] since the tournament expanded to 64 teams in 1985.{{cite news|first=Jonathan|last=Abrams|title=U.C.L.A. Is Trying to Send Gonzaga Back to 'Heartbreak City'|date=April 2, 2021|newspaper=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/02/sports/ncaabasketball/ucla-gonzaga-sweet-16.html|access-date=April 3, 2021}} The Bulldogs had been dominant all year, winning all but one of their 30 games by double digits,{{cite news|first=David|last=Cobb|title=2021 NCAA Final Four score: Gonzaga survives UCLA with buzzer-beater in OT, advances to national title game|date=April 4, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2021-ncaa-final-four-score-gonzaga-survives-ucla-with-buzzer-beater-in-ot-advances-to-national-title-game/live/|access-date=April 4, 2021}} including their last 27 straight.{{cite news|title=To the bank! Suggs hits the winner, Zags top UCLA 93-90|date=April 3, 2021|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401310867|access-date=April 4, 2021}} The game was close throughout and featured 19 lead changes and 15 ties.{{cite news|first=Adam|last=Grosbard|title=UCLA upset bid of Gonzaga foiled by Jalen Suggs' game winner|date=April 3, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/04/03/ucla-upset-bid-of-gonzaga-foiled-by-jalen-suggs-game-winner/|access-date=April 4, 2021}} The Bruins lost 93–90 in overtime after the Bulldogs' [[Jalen Suggs]] made a {{convert|40|ft|adj=on}} three-point [[bank shot (basketball)|bank shot]] as time expired.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA's title hopes shattered in Final Four loss to Gonzaga in overtime|date=April 3, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-04-03/ncaa-tournament-final-four-ucla-gonzaga-live-updates|access-date=April 3, 2021}} UCLA was the first opponent to hold a second-half lead against Gonzaga in the Bulldogs' first five games of the tournament. The game was the second most-watched tournament game of the season, behind the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]], with 14.94 million viewers and a 7.6 [[Nielsen ratings|TV rating]].{{cite web |last1=Paulsen |title=Nearly 17 million watch Baylor bully Bulldogs|url=https://www.sportsmediawatch.com/2021/04/march-madness-ratings-national-championship-baylor-gonzaga/|work=Sports Media Watch |date=April 7, 2021 |access-date=May 1, 2021}} ==Previous season== {{main|2019–20 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team}} UCLA finished the season with a 19–12 record. After starting slowly at 8–9, they went on an 11–3 streak and finished second in the Pac-12 at 12–6 in conference play. Cronin was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Coach of the Year|Pac-12 Coach of the Year]], while junior [[Chris Smith (basketball, born 1999)|Chris Smith]] earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors and was voted the Pac-12 Most Improved Player.{{cite news|last=Gold|first=Jon|title=A decade later, UCLA's Mick Cronin is following Sean Miller's playbook to rebuild Bruins|date=March 11, 2020|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/jon-gold-a-decade-later-ucla-s-mick-cronin-is/article_f49278a6-0f20-5090-ac87-03fe0cccb405.html|access-date=March 13, 2020}} Due to the coronavirus pandemic, the [[2020 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] was canceled before the Bruins' first scheduled game in the quarterfinals, and the [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] was called off as well. ==Off-season== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable sortable" style="text-align: center" |+ style="{{CollegePrimaryStyle|UCLA Bruins|color=white|border=no}}" | UCLA Departures |- align=center !
